papers.title: Simple methods to acutely measure multiple timing metrics among the sexual repertoire of male Drosophila.
papers.abstract: Male Drosophila courtship behavior is a key model for studying temporal decision-making. While courtship index (CI) is widely used to quantify mating activity, other timing metrics like courtship latency, copulation latency (CL), and mating duration (MD) remain understudied. Traditional methods for quantifying these behaviors are often labor-intensive and prone to human error. In this study, we present a protocol combining a modular chamber system and automated software (DrosoMating) to quantify six key timing metrics during male courtship. Our image-based video analysis enables precise identification of courtship and copulation events, as well as quantification of their timing and duration under controlled conditions. Validation shows <0.05% error rates and 98-99% agreement with manual scoring for CL, CI, and MD. The protocol supports genetic and neural circuit manipulations, detecting subtle genetic, social, and environmental behavioral variations. By minimizing manual effort and standardizing data collection, this approach facilitates scalable, reproducible studies on adaptive trade-offs, learning, and neural mechanisms in mating behavior. This method streamlines timing analysis in male courtship, offering reproducible metrics for behavioral genetics.

papers.title: Relationship Between Violence Against Children and Dating Violence Patterns Among Brazilian Adolescents: A Latent Class Analysis.
papers.abstract: Studies examining the associations between violence against children (VAC) and patterns of adolescent dating violence (DV) perpetration and victimization using person-centered analytic approaches remain limited and have yielded inconsistent findings. This study addresses whether emotional, physical, and sexual violence against children (VAC) are risk factors for distinct patterns of adolescent dating violence (DV), considering adolescents' gender and their roles as victims or perpetrators. This is a school based cross-sectional study that involved a stratified cluster sample of 550 s-year high school students from thirteen schools in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The Childhood Trauma Questionnaire (CTQ) was used to detect VAC, while DV was identified using the Brazilian version of the Conflict in Adolescent Dating Relationships Inventory (CADRI). Latent Class Analysis (LCA) was used to identify classes of individuals based on their response patterns to the CADRI items. Multinomial regression analysis examined the relationships between VAC and DV patterns. Among girls, no single type of VAC increased the odds of belonging to the most severe perpetration class of DV. However, childhood sexual abuse increased fivefold (OR: 5.72; 95% CI: 2.51-13.06) the likelihood of belonging to the most severe DV victimization class. Among boys, childhood emotional (OR: 1.65; 95% CI: 1.65 - 16.57) and physical abuse (OR: 2.66; 95% CI: 1.01 - 7.05) were associated with higher odds of DV perpetration. Emotional VAC increased boys' likelihood of belonging to the poly-victimization class (OR: 5.97; 95% CI: 1.95 - 18.30). Childhood physical abuse also increased their likelihood of belonging to severe class by more than three-fold (OR: 3.60; 95% CI: 1.80-7.21). The effects of childhood victimization on adolescent DV differ by sex, type of childhood violence, and whether the adolescent is a perpetrator or victim. papers.title: Childhood Trauma and Cyber Partner Aggression: The Indirect Effect of Maladaptive Schema in Indonesian Young Adults.
papers.abstract: As digital communication becomes central to modern relationships, it also creates new avenues for harm, one of which is cyber intimate partner aggression. In Indonesia, this digital form of partner violence appears to be increasing, particularly among young adults. This study examined how childhood trauma is associated with cyber aggression toward partners, and whether maladaptive schemas help account for this association. A diverse sample of young adults (N = 941; 84.5% women; Mage = 22.9, SD = 2.9) completed measures of Childhood Trauma Questionnaire-Short Form, the Young Schema Questionnaire-Short Form, and the Cyber Aggression in Relationship Scale. Controlling for relationship status and length, indirect effect analyses revealed that the disconnection and rejection schema, along with three of its subschemas (abandonment, mistrust/abuse, and self-isolation/alienation), accounted for part of the association between childhood trauma and cyber intimate partner aggression. Childhood trauma was associated with cyber intimate partner aggression both directly and indirectly through its association with disconnection and rejection schema. These findings highlight the disconnection and rejection schema as a psychological correlate linking childhood trauma to digital forms of partner aggression and suggest schema-based interventions as a promising direction for prevention and treatment.

papers.title: Self-Ratings, Partner Perceptions, and Ideal Partner Preferences of Gelotophobia, Gelotophilia, and Katagelasticism in Couples: Congruence and Associations With Relationship Satisfaction.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: How people deal with ridicule and being laughed at plays a role for romantic relationships. Gelotophobia (fear of being laughed at), gelotophilia (joy in being laughed at), and katagelasticism (joy in laughing at others) describe individual differences in dealing with laughter. We studied how differential perceptions among partners' traits and their profiles converge to address the description and effects of congruence. METHOD: We collected data from 286 opposite-gender couples (relationship duration: M = 6.8 years), who provided self- and partner ratings and ideal partner preferences for these laughter-related dispositions. We analyzed the congruence between different types of perceptions of the laughter-related dispositions and whether this congruence was associated with relationship satisfaction. We computed profile-based congruence analyses and conducted supplementary Dyadic Response Surface Analyses. RESULTS: We found that perceptions are interdependent within and between partners and that profile congruence between partner perceptions and ideal partner preferences is associated with greater relationship satisfaction above and beyond actor, partner, and stereotype effects. CONCLUSION: Self-, partner-, and ideal partner perceptions are differentially interrelated and congruence in their distinctive profiles relates to couples' satisfaction. We discuss the findings from the perspective of the Ideal Standards Model and encourage further research on perceptions less across traits.

papers.title: Association between clinical phenotypes and autoantibody profiles in idiopathic inflammatory myopathies: a Tunisian cohort study.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVES: Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIMs) are heterogeneous disorders characterized by variable muscular and extramuscular involvement. Myositis-specific autoantibodies (MSAs) have emerged as key tools for defining more homogeneous clinical subsets. This study aimed to investigate clinical-serological associations in a Tunisian cohort of patients with IIMs. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-center study including adult patients with MSA-positive IIMs fulfilling the 2017 ACR/EULAR classification criteria and/or anti-synthetase syndrome (ASyS) criteria. Clinical, biological, electromyographic, and histological data were analyzed according to serological subgroups: ASyS, dermatomyositis (DM)-specific antibodies, and anti-SRP immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM). RESULTS: Fifty patients were included (mean age 50.5 ± 12.9 years; 70% female). The most frequent subgroup was ASyS (n = 33), followed by DM (n = 10) and IMNM (n = 7). Interstitial lung disease (ILD) was most frequent in ASyS (85%), particularly associated with non-Jo-1 antibodies, while muscular involvement was less prominent compared to other groups. DM-specific antibodies were associated with a typical cutaneous phenotype, including heliotrope rash, Gottron's papules, and skin ulcerations, as well as higher frequency of dysphagia. Anti-SRP IMNM was characterized by severe and predominant muscle involvement, frequent dysphagia, and minimal extramuscular manifestations. No statistically significant difference in cancer prevalence was observed between groups, although a numerically higher frequency was noted in DM-associated antibodies. CONCLUSION: This Tunisian study highlights the clinical heterogeneity of IIMs and the close relationship between MSA profiles and clinical phenotypes. papers.title: Narratives about Breaking the Cycle of Intergenerational Violence in Families: Different Routes, Same Goal.
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Intergenerational violence in families is well documented, yet research often relies on quantitative methods, overlooking the complexity of lived experiences. Qualitative studies on parents exposed to both intimate partner violence (IPV) and child maltreatment remain scarce. This study examines narratives of Finnish parents to explore how parents with childhood experiences of both maltreatment and exposure to IPV narrate and make meaning of intergenerational continuity or change in violence. Data consist of 15 written narratives analyzed through narrative methods, including composite narratives and fictionalized characters to synthesize accounts and highlight thematic patterns. Our findings disrupt the notion of a simple, linear cycle of harm. Instead, intergenerational transmission emerges as a dynamic and probabilistic process. Breaking one cycle, such as IPV, does not automatically end another, like child maltreatment. What seems to matter is how individuals make sense of and integrate relational traumas into their life story. When these experiences are acknowledged and processed, parents can move toward earned secure attachment, transforming both parenting and partner relationships. Together these insights highlight the need for prevention strategies that go beyond exposure, focusing on early attachment support and interventions that combine personal agency and re-authoring childhood experiences with external resources such as safe relationships and professional guidance. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40653-026-00961-9.

papers.title: A bacterial chaperone-usher pathway links interkingdom association to antimicrobial protection of a fungal partner.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Antimicrobial compounds (AMCs) influence species-level composition of microbial communities, governing beneficial and pathogenic interactions with plant and mammalian hosts. Phenazine-1- carboxylic acid (PCA) is a bacterially produced, redox-active AMC abundant in the rhizosphere. A recent study discovered the PCA-susceptible fungus Aspergillus calidoustus can grow in PCA- abundant environments by associating with phenazine-tolerant bacteria, including the novel species Paraburkholderia edwinii . P. edwinii's protection response is characterized by adherence to its fungal partner, bacterial aggregation, and sequestration and reduction of PCA, rendering PCA less toxic. Deletion of the bacterial transcriptional repressor HrcA generates a constitutively active protection response and enhanced protection of A. calidoustus . Here, we use the Δ hrcA strain to determine whether fungal protection uses bacterial self-protection machinery or dedicated interkingdom mechanisms. We identified a divergent archaic chaperone-usher pathway (CUP) operon encoding a predicted periplasmic chaperone, outer membrane usher, putative major pilin-like subunit, and putative adhesin-like tip protein. While many archaic CUP operons are annotated in diverse bacteria, their functions remain largely unexplored. We show these f ungal a ttachment c omplex ( fac ) genes promote bacterial-fungal attachment, are required for P. edwinii to sequester and detoxify PCA, and contribute to full fungal protection from PCA stress, despite not being required for P. edwinii 's own tolerance of PCA. We further identified the transcription regulator, FacR, that influences expression of the fac system. Understanding the functions of divergent archaic CUP systems may illuminate protective interkingdom partnerships and inform how pathogenic and beneficial microbes gain entry to AMC-replete environments, shaping microbial communities in agricultural and clinical contexts. papers.title: Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework-67 Derived Nanoporous Carbon for Highly Efficient Effervescent Tablet-assisted Magnetic Solid-Phase Extraction of Clozapine and Its Metabolites in Human Urine Samples.
papers.abstract: A novel effervescent tablet based on zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF)-67-derived nanoporous carbon was fabricated and applied for simultaneous analysis of clozapine (CPZ) and its metabolites in human urine samples coupled with liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Adsorption experiments and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analysis revealed the affinity of ZIF-67-derived nanoporous carbon toward the analytes through π-π, hydrophobic, hydrogen bonding, and coordination interactions. Meanwhile, this sorbent exhibited excellent exclusion ability against interfering substances in urine samples. For the construction of the ZIF-67-derived nanoporous carbon-based effervescent tablet, both the tablet composition and the parameters affecting magnetic solid-phase extraction were optimized in detail. The proposed magnetic effervescent tablet enabled a fast adsorption process (∼5 min) and provided enhanced extraction efficiency (87.4%-98.3%) in a simple and convenient step. Coupled with LC-MS/MS, the developed method offered acceptable matrix effects of 0.98-1.00, wide linear ranges of 0.06-3000 ng/mL with correlation coefficients ≥0.9990, low detection limits of 0.02-0.30 ng/mL, and satisfactory recoveries of 91.1%-99.2%. In addition, the present approach allowed direct loading of crude urine samples without additional dilution and filtration steps, significantly simplifying the operation procedure. These results demonstrated an alternative strategy for highly efficient and convenient monitoring of CPZ and its metabolites in urine samples and proved the great application potential of ZIF-67-derived nanoporous carbon effervescent tablets for extracting pharmaceuticals from complex samples.

papers.title: Interface-Directed Two-Dimensional Growth of Non-Layered NiO on MoS2 Under Coupled External Fields.
papers.abstract: The controlled growth of two-dimensional (2D) non-layered transition metal oxides remains a key challenge in low-dimensional material synthesis. Achieving atomically precise construction of 2D structures requires a fundamental understanding of how external fields and interfacial interactions govern nucleation and growth processes. In this work, amorphous NiOx (a-NiOx) was deposited onto monolayer MoS2, and its transformation into crystalline 2D NiO nanosheets was directly visualized in situ using environmental transmission electron microscopy. The electron beam induces the decomposition of a-NiOx into mobile NiOx species, which migrate and nucleate on MoS2, demonstrating the synergistic roles of the electron beam and thermal field in NiO cluster formation and interface-dominated epitaxial growth. Combined notch-filtered imaging and theoretical calculations reveal that Ni-O units preferentially attach at the NiO/MoS2 interface to form one-dimensional growth fronts, while oriented attachment proceeds via nanosheet rotation, interfacial fusion, and defect-mediated reconstruction, culminating in lattice relaxation into a single-crystalline structure. High-throughput selected-area electron diffraction further uncovers the modulation of external fields on the multi-path structural evolution of NiOx. This work establishes an in situ strategy to resolve nucleation and growth pathways of 2D heterostructures, enabling active control over the 2D growth of non-layered metal oxides and advancing deterministic atomic-level construction.

papers.title: Magnetic Cu-based metal-organic framework/covalent organic framework composite for efficient extraction of Sudan dyes from fruit juice beverages.
papers.abstract: In this study, a new magnetic Cu-based metal-organic framework/covalent organic framework composite material (Fe3O4@PDA@HKUST-1@COF) was developed as an adsorbent for the extraction of Sudan dyes from fruit juice beverages. HKUST-1 provides Cu2+ coordination centers, while the COF component contributes a π-π conjugated system and residual -NH2 groups as hydrogen bond donors, synergistically enabling coordination, hydrogen bonding, and π-π stacking interactions for rapid adsorption equilibrium within 10 min. Based on the optimization of extraction conditions, magnetic solid-phase extraction was coupled with high-performance liquid chromatography-ultraviolet detector to establish a simple and sensitive method. The method exhibited satisfactory linearity over the concentration range of 0.5-500 µg L-1 (R2 > 0.999), with limits of detection of 0.07-0.12 µg L-1. Spike recoveries in fruit juice samples ranged from 83.0% to 102.0%, with relative standard deviations below 5.0%, indicating that this approach is suitable for detection of Sudan dyes in complex food matrices.

papers.title: The effects of angel sounds and guided imagery technique played to expectant couples on attachment, anxiety and sleep quality.
papers.abstract: The authors aimed to investigate the effects of listening to fetal heart sounds (FHS), metaphorically referred to as "angel sounds," and guided imagery technique (GIT) on prenatal attachment, anxiety, and sleep quality among expectant couples. A randomized controlled trial was conducted with nFHS = 59couples, nGIT = 59couples, and nControl = 59couples. Experimental group participants received nightly pre-sleep interventions for three consecutive nights. Fetal heart sounds were played for at least 20 min in the FHS group, and imaginary recordings containing different scenarios were played daily in the GIT group. Data were collected using Personal Information Forms, Maternal and Paternal Antenatal Attachment Scales, State Anxiety Inventory,and Richard-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire. FHS was more effective than GIT in reducing anxiety in women. FHS and GIT are effective non-pharmacological interventions for enhancing attachment and sleep quality in expectant couples (p < 0.05). These interventions may be integrated into routine prenatal care and offer a couple-centered approach to psychosocial support during pregnancy.

papers.title: An Antagonistic MdERF4-MdERF106 Switch Activates a MdWRKY33 Positive-Feedback Circuit to Drive Irreversible Ethylene-Induced Fruit Softening in Apple.
papers.abstract: Fruit softening represents a defining physiological transition of climacteric fruit ripening, yet the transcriptional mechanisms converting ethylene signalling into an irreversible developmental programme remain largely unresolved. In this study, we identify MdWRKY33 as a central hub linking ethylene signalling to cell wall remodelling during apple fruit softening. MdWRKY33 directly activates the cell wall-degrading enzyme gene MdPG, positively regulates its own transcription, and promotes ethylene production, thereby establishing a self-reinforcing regulatory circuit. Upstream of MdWRKY33, two ethylene-responsive transcription factors, MdERF4 and MdERF106, function antagonistically as a transcriptional repressor and activator, respectively. Ethylene coordinates this regulatory switch by suppressing MdERF4 while inducing MdERF106, thereby sustaining MdWRKY33 transcriptional activation and promoting rapid softening. Our findings reveal that an antagonistic ERF module is coupled with WRKY-mediated positive feedback to establish a robust transcriptional network that reinforces ethylene responses and drives irreversible commitment to the softening programme, providing mechanistic insights and potential targets for fruit quality improvement.

papers.title: The rollback of Māori rights in the context of health partnership, research and mental health legislation.
papers.abstract: This paper critiques recent policy and legislative developments in Aotearoa New Zealand, arguing that they represent a rollback of Māori rights in health, research and mental health law. The authors distinguish between inequality and inequity, emphasising that Māori experience disproportionate and avoidable disadvantages rooted in systemic factors. They challenge political narratives that frame equity-focussed approaches as race-based prioritisation, instead grounding their argument in Te Tiriti o Waitangi obligations and international human rights standards. The disestablishment of Te Aka Whai Ora - Māori Health Authority is identified as a key example of regression, with the United Nations Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination expressing concern that this decision undermines Indigenous rights and health equity. The paper further critiques the new Mental Health Act 2026, highlighting the continued reliance on compulsory community treatment and seclusion despite evidence demonstrating limited effectiveness and disproportionate impacts on Māori. Drawing on national and international research, the authors argue that coercive practices are inconsistent with human rights frameworks, including the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. They contend that the new legislation fails to deliver the transformational change envisaged in earlier policy commitments. As an alternative, the paper proposes the "community support commitment" model that would replace compulsory treatment with a rights-based, voluntary approach centred on supported decision making and service accountability. The paper concludes that without the legislation adopting the substantive reform required, current policy directions risk entrenching inequities and reversing progress towards equitable, culturally responsive and rights-based mental health care.

papers.title: Coalitional Formidability and Kinship Across Three Cultures : Experimentally Assessing Implications of Inclusive Fitness and Reciprocal Altruism.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: This study investigates how kinship composition shapes perceptions of coalitional formidability across three countries with different histories of kinship-based social organization. Inclusive fitness theory predicts that kin-based coalitions will be perceived as more formidable, at least on the dimensions closest to genuine altruism (Chapais, 2006). Reciprocal altruism theory (Trivers, 1971) predicts instead that familiar partners can sustain most coalitional cooperation regardless of relatedness, confining any kinship advantage to the costliest, least reciprocable commitments. We test these competing predictions. METHODS: We conducted a multilevel experimental study using vignettes depicting groups in conflict, sampling 613 participants from China (n = 204), the United States (n = 189), and India (n = 220). Participants rated coalitions described as kin-related or unrelated on seven operationalizations of coalitional formidability, which our framework sorts into four competence-dependent capability assessments (e.g., fighting skill, physical strength), two moderate-cost, reciprocable commitments (coordinated team play, standing one's ground), and one high-cost commitment, intra-group aid. Multilevel models estimated kinship effects while controlling for country and gender. RESULTS: The pre-registered omnibus test returned no overall kinship effect (b = - 0.024, p = .459; negative coefficients indicate higher ratings for kin-related coalitions). In exploratory dimension-specific models, kinship increased perceived willingness to provide intra-group aid (b = - 0.097, p = .005), the sole effect to survive Bonferroni correction. The four capability assessments showed no detectable kinship effects, and neither did the two commitment items on which inclusive-fitness reasoning had also predicted effects. papers.title: Income Instability During Pregnancy Prospectively Relates to Postpartum Brain Function for Parent-Infant Bonding.
papers.journal: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pregnancy represents a critical period of neuroplasticity when environmental stressors can disrupt the neurobiological foundations of parent-infant bonding, with lasting consequences for perinatal mental health. While chronic poverty has been linked to adverse parenting outcomes, the specific impact of income instability during pregnancy on parental brain adaptation remains unknown. METHODS: We examined whether prenatal income changes prospectively influence neurobiological responses to infant distress cues among birthing individuals (N = 120) during the early postpartum period. Monthly income data across pregnancy were used to compute income-to-needs ratio (INR), income losses, and income gains. Participants underwent functional magnetic resonance imaging while listening to their own and a control infant's cry and matched white noise. RESULTS: Income losses during pregnancy were associated with dampened brain responses to infant cry across motor, auditory, and empathy-related cortices-a pattern consistent with impaired caregiving sensitivity and known risk factors for postpartum depression. These neurobiological alterations were paralleled by elevated prenatal depression and anxiety symptoms. In contrast, income gains were associated with greater activation in response to one's own infant's cry in prefrontal regions involved in cognitive empathy and emotion regulation and were linked to stronger postnatal attachment bonds. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that prenatal income instability is associated with variation in postpartum brain responses within circuits relevant to caregiving and parent-infant bonding. The associations between prenatal income loss and prenatal mood symptoms also suggest that screening for economic instability during routine prenatal care may help identify families who could benefit from additional support, including mental health resources.

papers.title: The Impact of a Neurocollaborative Theraplay-informed Intervention on the Presentations of Developmental Trauma and Attachment Difficulties in Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder Children: A Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: The overlapping symptoms of ADHD, developmental trauma, and attachment difficulties in children complicate accurate assessment and intervention. Despite this, limited research has explored the efficacy of Theraplay for children with experiences of both ADHD and developmental trauma. This study evaluated the efficacy of a 30-hour, neuro-collaborative, Theraplay-informed intervention for looked-after children with ADHD, comparing outcomes to a non-ADHD control group. A mixed design was implemented, with two groups (ADHD and non-ADHD; N = 14 per group) participating between March 2019 and March 2024. The intervention included 10 h of therapeutic parenting based on Theraplay parent sessions and principles of dyadic developmental parenting, 10 h of family therapy based on the principles of Theraplay, and 10 h of sensory regulation work tailored to the child or family unit. Pre- and post-intervention outcomes were measured using the Assessment Checklist for Children (ACC), Behaviour Rating Inventory of Executive Functioning - 2nd Edition (BRIEF-2), Child Behaviour Checklist (CBCL), and Trauma Symptom Checklist for Young Children (TSCYC). Paired t-tests in the ADHD group revealed significant post-intervention reductions in CBCL total problems, rule-breaking behaviour, oppositional defiance, and TSCYC anxiety scores. Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) results found no significant differences between the ADHD and non-ADHD groups when controlling age, and gender, pre-test scores as covariates and post-test scores as the dependent variable. These findings suggest positive therapeutic outcomes for ADHD children with an improvement rate similar to their matched controls. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40653-026-00871-w.

papers.title: Graduate Family Therapy Training for First Nations Practitioners: Transformations of Self.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: In light of limited teaching resources and the essential need for Indigenous-focused learning material, this study sought to contribute to the development of culturally appropriate support for First Nations students training as family therapists. Drawing on the wisdom and experience of graduate students of an integrated family therapy training program that embeds Australian Aboriginal culture and Aboriginal wisdom within mainstream curriculum, we explore the transformative elements of course curriculum and teaching process. METHOD: As part of the course, First Nations students prepared reflective essays on their learnings related to culturally adapted systemic frameworks for working with Australian Indigenous families, including ethics of practice, and impacts for self. These essays (n = 9) were subject to grounded theoretical analysis. RESULTS: Findings highlight students' perceptions of the transformative impact of the graduate program on their personal and professional development. This impact was reflected across three key domains: (i) personal and professional growth, (ii) takeaway learnings, (iii) application of learning in family therapy practice. CONCLUSION: When taught within a culturally safe process, our findings show the powerful, recursive alignment of Indigenous ways of knowing and Western systemic approaches to family therapy. This integration is not only perceived as professionally enriching by students but also appears to support their personal growth and in turn their capacity to work respectfully and effectively with First Nations families. By embedding these respectful, integrated pedagogies into tertiary clinical training, students and supervisors can contribute to building sustainable practice capacity within First Nations communities, ultimately strengthening family and community wellbeing.

papers.title: The Relationship Between Postpartum Sexual Well-Being and Parenting Sense of Competence Among Mixed-Gender, First-Time Parent Couples.
papers.abstract: Although sexual well-being often declines during the transition to parenthood, little is known about how couples' sexual experiences relate to parental adjustment. Sexual satisfaction and sexual distress are central indicators of sexual well-being and may be associated with parents' perceptions of competence through spillover within individuals and crossover between partners. Guided by Family Systems Theory, this study examined associations between sexual satisfaction, sexual distress, and parenting sense of competence among first-time parent couples during the postpartum period. Participants were 132 mixed-gender first-time parent couples from Portugal assessed at three months postpartum. Associations between sexual satisfaction, sexual distress, and parenting sense of competence were examined using dyadic Actor-Partner Interdependence Models (APIM). The results indicated that greater sexual satisfaction was associated with men's own greater sense of parental competence, greater own sexual distress was associated with lower parental competence for both partners, and men's greater sexual distress was associated with women's lower parental competence. After adjustment for contextual variables, only the actor associations for men's sexual satisfaction and sexual distress remained statistically significant. These findings highlight the associations of sexual satisfaction and sexual distress with couples' adjustment to parenthood, particularly among new fathers, and suggest that sexual experiences and perceptions of parenting competence may represent interconnected aspects of adjustment during the postpartum period.

papers.title: Consensus Statements on Minimally Invasive Surgical Treatments for Male Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Secondary to Benign Prostatic Enlargement and Obstruction.
papers.journal: The world journal of men's health
papers.abstract: In recent times, scientific advances in male lower urinary tract symptoms (mLUTS) secondary to benign prostatic enlargement (BPE)/benign prostatic obstruction (BPO) technology, coupled with greater demands and awareness on preservation of sexual function in BPE/BPO surgery, have led to many patients seeking and urologists offering effective yet minimally invasive surgical treatments (MISTs). This modified Delphi consensus was initiated by the Male Lower Urinary Tract Advisory Group and key opinion leaders within the Urological Society of Australia and New Zealand to provide consensus statements and clinical recommendations to guide the current understanding and clinical care in this rapidly evolving field. Fourteen consensus statements are provided, along with corresponding levels of evidence and grades of recommendation, following a modified Delphi method. MIST should be offered to sexually active males with LUTS/BPE/BPO and patients who want surgery but wish to preserve fertility status for natural conception. Long-term clinical efficacy and safety data on MIST beyond 5 years are limited (except for prostatic urethral lift [PUL] or Urolift system). Almost all MIST preserve erectile function, although to date, only Urolift PUL system has consistently not been shown to cause ejaculatory dysfunction. There are very few direct comparative clinical trials among these minimally invasive BPE technologies, and few cost analysis studies comparing MIST with medical therapy, although MIST is likely to be more cost-effective than conventional transurethral resection of the prostate gland. Contemporary data on MIST shows effective and safe outcomes for mLUTS/BPE/BPO in the short-term. Patients should be counselled on specific advantages and limitations of individual MIST, with the choice of MIST likely determined and offered based on the patient's preference and prostate anatomy, the surgeon's expertise and availability of specific MIST technology locally.

papers.title: Just Not That Into You: Experiences of Indifference Toward a Romantic Partner.
papers.abstract: Theoretical work has proposed that people can have four different patterns of interpersonal evaluations: mostly positive, mostly negative, ambivalent (both positive and negative), and indifferent (neither positive nor negative). Notably, indifference has been largely overlooked by empirical research, despite growing evidence that indifferent feelings can occur in romantic relationships. To address this gap, we examined the associations of feelings of indifference toward one's romantic partner with relationship and personal well-being across four studies (N = 2,490), using cross-sectional and longitudinal data from couples and individuals in relationships. To do so, we developed the Subjective Interpersonal Indifference Scale and established it as a valid and reliable measure to assess this evaluation. Our findings showed that indifference toward a romantic partner is associated with lower relationship and personal well-being, both concurrently and longitudinally. Underlying these associations were higher feelings of boredom in the relationship, higher desire for attractive alternatives, and lower intimacy.

papers.title: From Sibling Violence to Intimate Partner Violence: The Role of Moral Disengagement.
papers.abstract: Sibling violence is one of the most common forms of family violence; however, it is frequently overlooked because it is often labeled as bullying, rivalry, or typical childhood conflict. As a result, harmful sibling interactions may be minimized despite evidence of their potential long-term consequences. The present study examined whether early experiences of sibling violence, including perpetration and victimization, were associated with intimate partner violence in adulthood and whether moral disengagement statistically accounted for indirect associations between these variables. Participants were 591 adults (77% female), aged 18 to 93 years, who retrospectively reported on childhood sibling experiences using the Sibling Bullying Scale. Intimate partner violence perpetration and victimization were assessed using the short form of the Psychological Maltreatment of Women Inventory, supplemented with items assessing physical aggression. Sibling violence was associated with intimate partner violence at the bivariate level, with more selective effects observed in multivariate models. Relational forms were particularly salient: sibling relational victimization showed the strongest direct associations with intimate partner violence victimization, whereas sibling relational perpetration was uniquely associated with moral disengagement. Moral disengagement was related to all intimate partner violence outcomes and mediated several pathways linking sibling relational perpetration to all intimate partner violence outcomes statistically accounted for several indirect associations between sibling relational perpetration and adult intimate partner violence, except for physical victimization. These findings suggest that forms of aggression often dismissed as normative may be associated with later relationship functioning and underscore the importance of recognizing sibling violence as a potential correlate of later intimate partner violence.

papers.title: Factors Associated With Violence by an Intimate Partner in Pregnant Women From the South of Brazil.
papers.abstract: Intimate partner violence (IPV) can result in physical, psychological or sexual harm. Thus, the objective of this study was to verify the factors associated with IPV in pregnant women in southern Brazil. A cross-sectional study was conducted using data from the research project entitled 'Mental health and living conditions of pregnant women receiving care in Primary Health Care', carried out with pregnant women attending Basic Health Units in the municipality of Criciúma, Santa Catarina, Brazil. IPV was assessed using the World Health Organization Violence Against Women questionnaire. A total of 353 pregnant women with intimate partners participated. Most were aged 20 to 29 years, white, living with a partner, and with 9 to 11 years of schooling. The majority reported a household income between 1.001 and 2.000 reais. Lifestyle characteristics revealed a small proportion of smokers, alcohol consumers, and physically active women. Regarding prenatal care, most attended six or more consultations, and more than half reported unplanned pregnancies. Overall, 13.6% of the women experienced IPV during pregnancy. Among the types of violence, psychological IPV was the most frequent (12.2%), followed by physical (3.1%) and sexual violence (3.1%). In crude analyses, younger age and low income were related to higher prevalence of IPV. Women with income ≤500 reais had significantly higher odds of suffering violence compared to those earning more than 2.000 reais. In the final adjusted model, income remained associated, with women in the lowest income category showing a 4.30-fold increased likelihood of experiencing IPV. These findings reinforce the role of socioeconomic vulnerability as a determinant of IPV during pregnancy. The findings show that IPV is present during pregnancy and point to low income as a risk factor for this outcome.

papers.title: The anatomy of female homicide: Psychiatric and criminal profiles of women offenders in Türkiye.
papers.abstract: Comparative data on the clinical and criminological profiles of female homicide offenders from non-Western jurisdictions remain scarce. This retrospective observational study characterised 112 consecutive female offenders referred between June 2018 and June 2023 to the Council of Forensic Medicine (Adli Tip Kurumu, ATK) of Türkiye the national-level referee body that provides binding forensic psychiatric opinions to all criminal courts, for intentional or attempted homicide, identifying independent predictors of full exemption from criminal responsibility under Article 32 of the Turkish Penal Code. The cohort (mean age 33.1 years) was predominantly of low educational attainment (71.5%) and unemployed (67.0%). Most offences occurred domestically (69.7%). Victims were primarily intra-familial, including the offenders' own children (42.0%, with neonates comprising a third of child victims), intimate partners (21.4%), and other relatives or non-relatives (36.6%). Nearly half (49.1%) had a documented pre-offence psychiatric diagnosis. Ultimately, 16.1% were adjudicated non-responsible; all of these cases involved psychotic-spectrum diagnoses or excitative/peripartum states, namely acute manic and postpartum psychotic episodes. Multivariable logistic regression demonstrated that active delusions at the time of the offence (aOR 48.0) and a pre-existing psychiatric diagnosis (aOR 8.7) strongly predicted legal exemption, whereas filicide paradoxically served as a negative predictor (aOR 0.14). Exploratory k-means cluster analysis suggested two tentative, hypothesis-generating typologies, a "filicide-reactive" group and a "psychotic/non-domestic" group, with the latter exhibiting a 4.5-fold higher rate of criminal exemption. These findings indicate that active psychotic symptomatology, rather than the specific victim-offender relationship, dictates criminal non-responsibility. papers.title: Wounded Boys, Violent Men? Exploring Risk Factors for Intimate Partner Violence among Perpetrators with a History of Trauma.
papers.abstract: One of the key challenges for enhancing the effectiveness of intervention programs for intimate partner violence (IPV) perpetrators is tailoring interventions to participants' specific risks and needs. A history of childhood or adolescent exposure to family violence as either a direct victim or witness has been consistently associated with an increased risk of IPV perpetration in adulthood. This study examined differences between 1,126 court-mandated male IPV perpetrators with and without a history of family violence exposure during childhood or adolescence across sociodemographic, individual, social-relational, attitudinal, and violence-related variables. The study also examined whether trauma history was associated with IPV recidivism risk beyond sociodemographic characteristics and after accounting for individual, social-relational, and attitudinal factors. Compared to perpetrators without trauma exposure, those with a trauma history were younger, had lower educational attainment, included a higher proportion of immigrant participants, and reported higher impulsivity, anger, depressive symptoms, alexithymia, and substance use. They also reported more stressful life events, lower perceived family and friend support, and higher hostile sexism and victim-blaming attitudes. In addition, they reported greater physical and psychological IPV, a more advanced stage of change, and higher risk of IPV recidivism at intake. Hierarchical logistic regression analyses showed that younger age, unemployment, higher impulsivity, and lower perceived family social support were the variables most strongly associated with trauma history. Hierarchical linear regression analyses further revealed that trauma history remained significantly associated with IPV recidivism risk after accounting for covariates. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating trauma-informed strategies into IPV perpetrator interventions.

papers.title: Intimate Partner Violence Among Sexual Minority Men in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: While extant scholarship has identified intimate partner violence (IPV) as a pervasive public health concern, most research has largely centered heterosexual relationships, leaving the experiences of sexual minority men (SMM) underexamined, particularly in low- and middle-income settings. In Sub-Saharan Africa, criminalization of same-sex relationships, structural stigma, and limited access to affirming services may uniquely shape IPV risk and related outcomes among SMM. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized evidence on the prevalence, correlates, and health outcomes of IPV among SMM in Sub-Saharan Africa. Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, we identified 17 eligible studies across 9 countries. Random-effects meta-analyses estimated pooled prevalence of IPV victimization and perpetration, and thematic synthesis summarized multilevel risk factors and health consequences. The pooled prevalence of any IPV victimization was 20% (95% CI [13%, 29%]), and the pooled prevalence of IPV perpetration was 16% (95% CI [6%, 29%]), with substantial heterogeneity across studies. IPV prevalence was higher in West Africa than in Southern Africa and in studies using recall periods longer than 12 months. IPV was associated with adverse mental health outcomes, substance use, sexual risk behaviors, and increased vulnerability to HIV and other sexually transmitted infections. Multilevel risk factors included childhood adversity, relationship power imbalances, economic dependence, stigma, and structural discrimination. Significant gaps remain, including limited geographic coverage, inconsistent IPV measurement, and a lack of intervention-focused research. Addressing IPV among SMM in Sub-Saharan Africa is critical for advancing health equity and requires contextually tailored prevention and response strategies that address both interpersonal violence and the broader structural conditions shaping vulnerability.

papers.title: A Qualitative Scoping Review of the Impact of Migration on Experiences of Intimate Partner Violence Among Latinas.
papers.abstract: Intimate partner violence (IPV) has several negative consequences in different life realms. Immigration can be a risk factor for women experiencing IPV, as survivors may lose protective factors such as access to protection services. This study aimed to conduct a scoping review of qualitative research to investigate post-migration barriers and challenges faced by Latin American immigrant women experiencing IPV. Qualitative papers were selected from 2019 to 2025 through Science Direct, Sage, Web of Science, Lilacs, Pubmed/Medline, SciELO, PePsic, and PsycINFO databases in English, Portuguese, and Spanish. We identified 23 studies, which revealed that structural and sociocultural hurdles, including a lack of documentation, fear of deportation, language barriers, and social isolation, mark the post-migration experience. Still, women demonstrate resilience and seek community support and specialized services, even in the most adverse conditions. Scholars and practitioners must develop intervention programs tailored to the migratory context of these women to guarantee their rights and promote their autonomy.

papers.title: Double Burden: Anxiety Symptoms and Chronic Conditions Compound Poor Health Outcomes Among Survivors of Intimate Partner Violence.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Experiencing intimate partner violence (IPV) is linked to poorer health and wellbeing, yet the interplay between physical and psychological comorbidities remains underexplored. This study evaluates the compounded burden of chronic illness and anxiety on self-perceived health in a national cohort of IPV survivors. METHODS: Fifteen thousand nine hundred forty-seven participants in the NIH All of Us database with accessible medical records who reported experiencing IPV answered questions from validated questionnaires about anxiety history, perceived overall health, and social satisfaction. Four groups were established: controls, high anxiety and a chronic condition, only high anxiety, and only a chronic condition. Chronic conditions were based on SNOMED codes (e.g., HTN, DM, COPD, and autoimmune conditions). Weighted propensity scores balanced cohorts based on age, sex, education, and race/ethnicity. Proportional odds logistic regressions predicted the odds of reporting negative overall health and social satisfaction based on exposure group. RESULTS: Compared to controls, IPV survivors with both high anxiety and a chronic condition had greater odds of reporting worse overall health (OR = 3.30, 95% CI [3.01-3.63]) and lower social satisfaction (OR = 2.11, [1.92-2.31]). Those with either high anxiety or a chronic disease, to a lesser degree, reported worse overall health (OR [1.34(1.22-1.48), 2.28(2.03-2.56)] and lower social satisfaction (OR [1.52(1.38-1.66), 1.26(1.12-1.41)]. CONCLUSIONS: Anxiety symptoms and chronic illness are strongly associated with poorer perceived health and social satisfaction among IPV survivors. While each comorbidity negatively impacted perceived health, their combined burden conferred the greatest risk. papers.title: Sapphires and Superwomen: The Role of Ambivalent Sexism, Religiosity and Internalized Racism on Attitudes Toward Intimate Partner Violence.
papers.abstract: Grounded in misogynoir and ambivalent sexism theories, this study explores how gendered stereotypes (Sapphire and Superwoman), internalized racism, sexist beliefs and religiosity are associated with attitudes toward intimate partner violence (IPV) among African individuals. Despite growing research on IPV, less is known about how stereotypes specific to Black women relate to IPV attitudes in sub-Saharan African contexts, where postcolonial dynamics and religiosity may shape these associations differently from Western contexts. This study addresses that gap by examining how both hostile and benevolent forms of sexism, as well as internalized racism and religiosity, are associated with more permissive attitudes toward IPV. We surveyed 184 students hailing from regions in sub-Saharan Africa, predominantly Nigeria (55.4% women, 44.6% men). Correlational and gender-stratified hierarchical regression analyses indicated that internalized racism was consistently associated with more permissive IPV attitudes among both men and women. Hostile sexism remained a significant predictor among men, whereas religiosity was associated with less permissive IPV attitudes and remained significant among women. By extending racialized gender stereotype research beyond Western contexts, the study highlights the importance of cultural specificity in understanding the complex ways oppression manifests within Black communities.

papers.title: Hombre a Hombre: Results from a Feasibility Study of an Adapted Relationship Education Program for HIV Prevention Among Latino Sexual Minority Men.
papers.abstract: Latino sexual minority men (LSMM) experience HIV health disparities and co-occurring intimate partner violence, depression, and substance use disparities that worsen HIV-related outcomes. One possibility for addressing these co-occurring health concerns among LSMM through a common intervention point could be strengthening LSMM's romantic and sexual relationship skills. The purpose of this study was to assess the acceptability, appropriateness, feasibility, and preliminary outcomes of Hombre a Hombre (HaH), a culturally adapted relationship education program delivered to a group of LSMM (N = 16). Quantitative assessments indicated HaH was highly acceptable and appropriate (all rating above the "agree" anchor point). We explored intervention outcomes, which non-significantly shifted in the expected direction for relationship outcomes (e.g., sexual agreement self-efficacy) and minority stress/resilience outcomes (e.g., internalized homonegativity, community connectedness). Participants reported high engagement with biomedical prevention/treatment at all time points, limiting our ability to detect changes across time. Exit interview themes underscored the acceptability and appropriateness of HaH for LSMM, while also identifying opportunities to culturally adapt the program to a greater extent, refine the program's structure, and support peer facilitators. Overall, this initial study suggests HaH's promise for potential sexual health impacts on LSMM via theoretically linked constructs. The study also informed refinements that could enhance HaH's impact a fully powered trial focused on LSMM with HIV acquisition or transmission risk.Clinical Trial Registry This study was registered with clinicaltrials.gov (NCT06056661) on September 20, 2023. papers.title: Perceived connection and similarity to the deceased as predictors of psychopathological adjustment following suicide loss.
papers.abstract: Suicide bereavement is associated with an increased risk of adverse mental health outcomes. While demographic and loss-related risk factors have been identified, little is known about the role of the perceived relationship quality with the deceased. 193 adults bereaved by suicide completed questionnaires assessing prolonged grief disorder (PGD), (complex) posttraumatic stress disorder (c/PTSD), disturbances in self-organization (DSO), depression, suicidal ideation, and Simpatico. Hierarchical regression analyses examined whether Simpatico predicted mental health outcomes beyond sociodemographic and loss-related characteristics. Exploratory analyses examined perceived understanding and comfort in sharing grief-related thoughts and feelings with family and friends. Greater felt similarity was associated with higher PGD and depression symptoms, and suicidal ideation, whereas greater felt connection was associated with lower symptoms in these domains. The perceived relationship quality with the deceased may contribute to psychological adjustment following suicide loss beyond established factors.
